coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a tendency to support or oppose someone or something unfairly
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The news report showed a clear bias towards one side of the argument.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: words that show a strong opinion and are not fair or neutral
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The writer used biased language such as 'useless' to describe the opposing plan.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: words that show balanced, objective opinion and free from bias
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: News reports must use neutral language when covering complex social topics.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: التحفظ في الكلام / عبارات تقلل من درجة التأكيد
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: using careful language to avoid making a statement sound too certain
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Scientific papers use hedging words like 'may' and 'indicate' to avoid premature conclusions.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the tendency to post only the best moments online, creating a false image of reality
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Social media creates a highlight-reel effect where people only showcase their successes.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: evaluating yourself by comparing yourself to others
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Constant social comparison online often leads to lowered self-esteem among adolescents.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: الانعكاس الاجتماعي / رؤية الشخص لنفسه من خلال نظرة الآخرين
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the way people understand or judge themselves through other people's reactions, opinions, and feedback
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Social reflection shapes how young people define their values and public personas.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: صفة تقييمية / صفة تعبر عن رأي أو حكم
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: an adjective that expresses a judgment or opinion (e.g. amazing, toxic, unrealistic)
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Words like 'flawless' and 'terrible' are evaluative adjectives carrying emotional weight.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: سؤال بلاغي / سؤال لا ينتظر منه إجابة
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a question asked to make a point or create an effect, not to get an answer
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Do we really want algorithms to control how we feel about our lives?

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the process of developing a sense of who you are and what you believe
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Teenage years are a crucial stage for authentic identity formation.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a word that makes the meaning of another word stronger
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The word 'extremely' in 'extremely difficult' is an intensifier.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the way you value and respect yourself
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Encouragement from mentors significantly boosts a student's self-esteem.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: الصورة الذاتية / تصور الشخص عن نفسه
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the mental picture or opinion a person has about their own appearance, abilities, personality, and value
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Filtered photos can distort a teenager's self-image and perception of beauty.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: choosing only certain things, or people instead of everything
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Curated social accounts present a very selective view of an individual's lifestyle.

languageNotes.note: Affect is usually a verb, whereas effect is usually a noun.

languageNotes.meaningA: حساس / سريع التأثر بالمشاعر أو البيئة
languageNotes.note: Sensitive relates to emotions and reactions, while sensible denotes wisdom and sound judgment.
Use 'balanced' as an adjective before nouns like 'diet' or 'lifestyle'.

languageNotes.meaningA: ينشر (شخص أو دار نشر تطرح كتاباً أو مقالاً)
languageNotes.note: A publisher publishes a book; a book comes out.
Power is the abstract noun; powerful modifies nouns that possess strong agency.

mcq.questionText: Constant social comparison made Ahmed feel that his life was less successful than the lives he saw online. What does 'social comparison' mean in this context?
options: Judging yourself by comparing your life with other people's lives.
Studying the traditions of different societies.
mcq.correctAnswer: Judging yourself by comparing your life with other people's lives.
mcq.explanation: Social comparison refers to the psychological process of evaluating one's own achievements and value against others.

mcq.questionText: A podcast host invited only guests who agreed with his views and dismissed opposing opinions without discussing them fairly. Listeners described the program as biased. Which situation is the clearest example of being 'biased'?
options: A judge scores every performance according to the same published rules.
A judge gives a friend a higher score even though another performer clearly did better.
A judge asks another official to review a result that is extremely close.
A judge changes a score after noticing a genuine mistake in the first calculation.
mcq.correctAnswer: A judge gives a friend a higher score even though another performer clearly did better.
mcq.explanation: Bias means showing unfair favoritism towards one person or perspective over another.

mcq.questionText: Mariam posts only photos of holidays, celebrations, and achievements, so her followers imagine that her life is always perfect. This creates a highlight-reel effect. Which situation is the clearest example of the 'highlight-reel effect'?
options: A student shares both successes and failures during a difficult school year.
A traveller posts only luxury hotels and exciting trips while hiding stressful moments.
A teacher uploads full lessons so students can review their mistakes.
A family discusses both positive and negative events openly at home.
mcq.correctAnswer: A traveller posts only luxury hotels and exciting trips while hiding stressful moments.
mcq.explanation: The highlight-reel effect occurs when someone selectively curates and showcases only ideal, glamorous events while omitting struggles.

mcq.questionText: The writer used biased language such as 'terrible' and 'completely useless' when describing the plan. What does 'biased language' mean in this context?
options: Words used only in scientific reports.
Words that show a strong opinion and are not fair or neutral.
Words that make information easier to memorize.
Words used to introduce several different viewpoints.
mcq.correctAnswer: Words that show a strong opinion and are not fair or neutral.
mcq.explanation: Biased language relies on subjective, charged adjectives rather than objective, balanced evidence.

mcq.questionText: A news report should use neutral language when presenting different sides of an argument. What does 'neutral language' mean in this context?
options: Language that strongly supports one side.
Language that deliberately hides important facts.
Language that is balanced, objective, and free from bias.
Language that contains emotional and exaggerated expressions.
mcq.correctAnswer: Language that is balanced, objective, and free from bias.
mcq.explanation: Neutral language avoids emotional coloring and maintains fairness across all perspectives.

mcq.questionText: Instead of saying, 'This method will definitely work,' Mona wrote, 'This method may be effective.' This use of careful language is called ......... .
mcq.explanation: Hedging is the practice of using modal verbs like 'may' or 'might' to avoid making overly rigid claims.

mcq.questionText: In the sentence 'Social media creates a toxic environment,' the word 'toxic' expresses the writer's judgment. 'Toxic' is an example of a/an ......... .
mcq.explanation: Evaluative adjectives convey personal qualitative judgments (such as toxic, harmful, or wonderful).

mcq.questionText: People sometimes post only holidays, successes, and perfect moments online, giving others an incomplete picture of their lives. This is known as the ......... .
mcq.explanation: Curating solely peak positive moments creates the classic highlight-reel distortion.

mcq.questionText: In the phrase 'extremely difficult,' the word 'extremely' is an intensifier. What does 'intensifier' mean in this context?
options: A word that reduces the certainty of a statement.
A word that makes the meaning of another word stronger.
A word that introduces an opposite idea.
A word that makes a statement more neutral.
mcq.correctAnswer: A word that makes the meaning of another word stronger.
mcq.explanation: Intensifiers (like extremely, completely, very) scale up the magnitude of adjectives and adverbs.

mcq.questionText: The writer asked, 'Do we really want technology to control our lives?' What does 'rhetorical question' mean in this context?
options: A question asked to check factual information.
A question requiring a detailed written answer.
A question used to test someone's knowledge.
A question asked to make a point rather than get an answer.
mcq.correctAnswer: A question asked to make a point rather than get an answer.
mcq.explanation: A rhetorical question serves an illustrative or persuasive purpose to engage critical thinking without requiring a literal reply.

mcq.questionText: In the phrase 'deeply disappointed' the word 'deeply' makes the feeling of disappointment stronger. Which sentence contains the clearest example of an 'intensifier'?
options: The students were incredibly excited about the competition.
The students might attend the event tomorrow.
mcq.correctAnswer: The students were incredibly excited about the competition.
mcq.explanation: 'Incredibly' is an intensifier strengthening 'excited'.

mcq.questionText: Describing one group as 'wonderful' and another as 'useless' is ......... .
mcq.explanation: Using polarized judgmental adjectives is biased language.

mcq.questionText: News reports should use ......... when presenting different sides of an argument.
mcq.explanation: Neutral language ensures unbiased reporting.

mcq.questionText: Using words such as 'may' and 'might' to avoid certainty is called ......... .
mcq.explanation: Hedging tones down overgeneralization.

mcq.questionText: Posting only holidays and successes online can create the ......... .
mcq.explanation: Highlight-reel effect specifically describes showing only optimal moments.

mcq.questionText: Developing beliefs, values, and a sense of who you are is ......... .
mcq.explanation: Identity formation is the internal construction of one's core self and principles.

mcq.questionText: The way people judge themselves through others' reactions means ......... .
mcq.explanation: Social reflection is viewing one's worth through the mirror of external social perceptions.

mcq.questionText: Although he had achieved a lot, constant comparison left him feeling unhappy with his life. This feeling of ......... made him focus only on what he lacked.
mcq.explanation: Dissatisfaction reflects constant discontent with one's situation.

mcq.questionText: 'Many customers expressed dissatisfaction with the poor quality of the service.' The underlined noun is closest in meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Discontent is an exact synonym of dissatisfaction.

mcq.questionText: 'Expecting every student to achieve perfect marks is unrealistic.' The underlined adjective has an antonymous meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Reasonable is an antonym for unrealistic.

mcq.questionText: 'The speaker used a rhetorical question to make the audience think deeply.' The underlined adjective is closest in meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Rhetorical questions act persuasively on the listener's thought process.

mcq.questionText: 'The teacher used examples to highlight the most important points.' The underlined verb is closest in meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Highlight means to emphasize or underline importance.

mcq.questionText: 'The scientist used hedging when he said the results might indicate a connection.' The underlined noun has an antonymous meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Hedging denotes caution and avoidance of absolute certainty; hence certainty is its direct antonym.

mcq.questionText: 'Technology can transform the way students learn and communicate.' The underlined verb has an antonymous meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Preserve means to keep unchanged, contrasting with transform (to change deeply).

mcq.questionText: 'The article was biased because it presented only one side of the argument.' The underlined adjective is closest in meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Partial means taking a side unfairly; biased.

mcq.questionText: 'The athletes continued training despite the intense heat.' The underlined adjective has an antonymous meaning to ......... .
mcq.explanation: Mild (moderate, gentle) is the antonym of intense.

mcq.questionText: Instagram is mainly a/an ......... platform where users share photos.
mcq.explanation: An image-based platform prioritizes photos and visual media.

mcq.questionText: The report was ......... because it mentioned only the evidence supporting one side.
mcq.explanation: Selective means choosing only specific data to paint an incomplete picture.

mcq.questionText: Receiving encouragement can improve a teenager's confidence and ......... .
mcq.explanation: Encouragement directly supports healthy self-esteem.

mcq.questionText: Expecting every student to achieve perfect results without making mistakes is ......... .
mcq.explanation: Expecting flawlessness is unrealistic.

mcq.questionText: I know Hany slightly from work; he is only a/an ......... .
mcq.explanation: An acquaintance is someone known slightly, not intimately.

mcq.questionText: Employees in ......... industries need to update their skills regularly.
mcq.explanation: Rapidly evolving fields are described as fast-changing.

mcq.questionText: Early experiences can ......... the way children think about themselves.
mcq.explanation: Shape means to mold or influence fundamentally.

mcq.questionText: Regular criticism made Salma doubt her abilities and lowered her ......... .
mcq.explanation: Criticism harms personal self-esteem.

mcq.questionText: Modern technology can ......... traditional classrooms into interactive learning environments.
mcq.explanation: Transform implies deep structural conversion.

mcq.questionText: Young children can be particularly ......... to criticism from adults.
mcq.explanation: Sensitive to criticism means vulnerable and easily affected.

mcq.questionText: Better training can reduce the ......... between workers' skills and job requirements.
mcq.explanation: Skills gap is the difference between requirements and capabilities.

mcq.questionText: Students may feel ......... pressure before important exams.
mcq.explanation: Intense pressure denotes severe psychological strain.

mcq.questionText: Regular exercise helps people ......... good physical and mental health.
mcq.explanation: Maintain means to preserve or keep up.

mcq.questionText: A healthy lifestyle requires a/an ......... combination of work, rest, and exercise.
mcq.explanation: A balanced combination brings equilibrium across routines.

mcq.questionText: The neutral report will ......... the main causes of air pollution in cities.
mcq.explanation: Highlight means to feature prominently.

mcq.questionText: The manager rejected the employee's ......... behaviour towards customers.
mcq.explanation: Aggressive behavior is hostile and unprofessional.

mcq.questionText: ......... his older brother, Karim prefers working alone rather than in teams.
mcq.explanation: Unlike introduces a contrast between two individuals.

mcq.questionText: Sadly, people often ......... their real lives ......... the polished lives shown online.
mcq.explanation: The prepositional phrase is 'compare something to something'.

mcq.questionText: Social media can become a ......... where users display only their best moments.
mcq.explanation: A 'highly curated stage' refers to presenting an artfully filtered persona.

mcq.questionText: Even after facing several difficulties, she decided to ......... working toward her goal.
mcq.explanation: 'Go on' is a phrasal verb meaning to continue.

correctForm.prompt: Scientists must ......... (identity) the main causes of climate change.
correctForm.explanation: After the modal verb 'must', the base form of the verb 'identify' is required.

correctForm.prompt: The report highlighted a clear ......... (transform) in teenagers' self-image.
correctForm.explanation: The adjective 'clear' modifies the noun form 'transformation'.

correctForm.prompt: Many students found it hard to stay ......... (satisfy) with their achievements after comparing themselves with others.
correctForm.explanation: Stay + adjective requires the participle adjective 'satisfied'.

correctForm.prompt: It is useful to ......... (comparison) different sources before trusting a piece of news.
Social media has a strong ......... (influential) on how teenagers view themselves.
The teacher gave instructions on how to ......... (formation) a strong argument in an essay.
In the ......... (compare) paragraph, students must show similarities and differences.
correctForm.explanation: Modifying the noun 'paragraph' requires the adjective 'comparative'.

correctForm.prompt: The customer expressed her ......... (satisfy) with the quality of the product.
Her ......... (select) of words in the speech made it very persuasive.
Psychologists say celebrities can be extremely ......... (influence) on people's behavior.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following is an intensifier?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Extremely' strengthens the degree of an adjective.

skillsWriting.questionText: What is the main effect of a rhetorical question?
skillsWriting.explanation: Rhetorical questions stimulate active audience engagement.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which persuasive technique is used in the sentence, 'Do we really want to live in a world full of pollution?'
skillsWriting.explanation: It poses a dramatic query that highlights a shared value without expecting a literal answer.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a rhetorical question?
options: Could this really be the best solution?
skillsWriting.correctAnswer: Could this really be the best solution?
skillsWriting.explanation: It questions the consensus to provoke thought.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following is an intensifier?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Significantly' is an adverb used as an intensifier.

skillsWriting.questionText: What is the main effect of using hedging words?
skillsWriting.explanation: Hedging displays academic modesty and caution.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following is an absolute word?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Always' is an absolute word leaving no exceptions.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which persuasive technique is used here: 'We could possibly find a better solution.'?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Could possibly' shows cautious hedging.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a hedging word?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Totally' is an absolute intensifier, not a hedging word.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which of the following contains an intensifier?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Extremely' is an intensifier.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which persuasive technique is used here: 'Nobody should be treated unfairly'?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Nobody' is an absolute pronoun.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which word expresses uncertainty rather than complete confidence?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Possibly' signals probability rather than certainty.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which word is used to make the meaning of an adjective stronger?
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Extremely' functions as a degree intensifier.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which persuasive technique is used in the sentence: 'Who wouldn't want to live in a clean environment?'?
skillsWriting.explanation: It appeals to self-evident common values through a rhetorical query.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which sentence uses the most neutral language?
options: All young people waste too much time on their phones.
Teenagers are completely addicted to technology.
Some young people may spend considerable time using digital devices.
Everyone knows smartphones are ruining teenagers' lives.
skillsWriting.correctAnswer: Some young people may spend considerable time using digital devices.
skillsWriting.explanation: It avoids sweeping generalizations like 'all', 'completely', or 'ruining'.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which sentence uses hedging language most effectively?
options: Video games definitely cause aggressive behavior.
Video games always make children more aggressive.
Certain types of video games may influence aggressive behavior in some players.
Everyone who plays violent games eventually becomes aggressive.
skillsWriting.correctAnswer: Certain types of video games may influence aggressive behavior in some players.
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Certain types', 'may influence', and 'in some players' are precise, calibrated hedges.

skillsWriting.questionText: Which statement is an example of biased language?
options: Some research suggests that sleep can influence academic performance.
Students may need different amounts of sleep depending on several factors.
Teenagers who stay up late are irresponsible and do not care about school.
Insufficient sleep may affect concentration in some students.
skillsWriting.correctAnswer: Teenagers who stay up late are irresponsible and do not care about school.
skillsWriting.explanation: Labeling teenagers as 'irresponsible' and attributing negative intent is biased and judgmental.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a state of being comfortable, healthy, and happy
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Physical activity and social connection are vital for holistic well-being.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: paying careful attention to the present moment without distraction
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Practicing daily mindfulness helps reduce stress and improve mental focus.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: involving little physical movement and spending much time seated
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: A sedentary lifestyle has been directly linked to numerous chronic health problems.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: مُقدّر بأقل من قيمته الحقيقية / مهمل الأثر
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: not valued enough or assumed to be smaller or less significant than it really is
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The impact of adequate sleep on academic memory is often underestimated.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: noticeable or able to be tracked, counted, or verified
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Regular exercise yields measurable reductions in resting heart rate.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the practice of paying careful attention to what, why, and how much you consume
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Mindful consumption applies to both the food we eat and the online content we absorb.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the relationships and interactions people share with others
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Genuine social connections protect individuals from severe loneliness.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the process of getting the food and nutrients needed for health and growth
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Proper adolescent nutrition fuels rapid brain development.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a health expert who gives advice on what to eat to stay healthy
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The school consulted a nutritionist to design wholesome cafeteria lunches.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: any food altered from its natural state, often with added sugar, salt, or chemicals
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Diets rich in ultra-processed food increase risk of energy fatigue.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: wanting to compete successfully or being better than others
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: High school exams can foster an intensely competitive atmosphere.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a serious mental health condition causing persistent sadness and loss of interest
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Clinical depression requires professional empathy and medical counseling.

languageNotes.note: A biological or mental process vs a medical surgical operation.

mcq.questionText: After improving her sleep, diet, and relationships, Hind noticed a clear improvement in her well-being. What does 'well-being' mean in this context?
options: The state of being healthy, comfortable and happy.
The ability to become famous online.
The habit of avoiding all responsibilities.
The process of comparing yourself with others.
mcq.correctAnswer: The state of being healthy, comfortable and happy.
mcq.explanation: Well-being encompasses positive holistic health, comfort, and happiness.

mcq.questionText: During the relaxation session, Youssef practiced mindfulness by noticing his breathing, thoughts, and feelings without becoming distracted. What does 'mindfulness' mean in this context?
options: Comparing your life with other people's lives.
Paying careful attention to the present moment.
mcq.correctAnswer: Paying careful attention to the present moment.
mcq.explanation: Mindfulness means focusing attention intentionally on the current moment.

mcq.questionText: After changing his daily routine, eating better, and spending more time with family, Omar noticed a clear improvement in his well-being. Which situation is the clearest example of improved 'well-being'?
options: A student studies for longer hours but sleeps less every night.
A worker earns more money but feels constantly exhausted and stressed.
A person feels healthier, calmer, and happier after improving daily habits.
A teenager spends more time online comparing himself with others.
mcq.correctAnswer: A person feels healthier, calmer, and happier after improving daily habits.
mcq.explanation: True well-being is manifested in feeling healthy, calm, and balanced.

mcq.questionText: The company needed measurable results so managers could track progress clearly using numbers and data. What does 'measurable' mean in this context?
options: Able to be tracked, counted, or clearly noticed.
mcq.correctAnswer: Able to be tracked, counted, or clearly noticed.
mcq.explanation: Measurable means quantifiable through data.

mcq.questionText: Regular conversations with friends gave Karim a stronger sense of social connection and helped him feel less isolated. What does 'social connection' mean in this context?
options: The process of using social media for business.
The relationships and interactions people have with others.
The habit of studying other societies.
The tendency to avoid meeting people.
mcq.correctAnswer: The relationships and interactions people have with others.
mcq.explanation: Social connection refers to interpersonal bonds and mutual support.

mcq.questionText: During a stressful school day, Salma practiced mindfulness by stopping for a few minutes and focusing only on her breathing and present thoughts. Which situation is the clearest example of 'mindfulness'?
options: A student avoids thinking about any feelings or emotions.
A student keeps thinking about mistakes made several months ago.
A student compares his results with everyone else in the class.
A student quietly notices his breathing instead of worrying about his exam.
mcq.correctAnswer: A student quietly notices his breathing instead of worrying about his exam.
mcq.explanation: Observing one's present breath grounds awareness in the moment.

mcq.questionText: Ahmed is highly competitive and always tries to perform better than his classmates and win every contest. What does 'competitive' mean in this context?
options: Wanting to compete successfully or be better than others.
Preferring to work alone without goals.
mcq.correctAnswer: Wanting to compete successfully or be better than others.
mcq.explanation: Competitive people strive vigorously for victory and superiority.

mcq.questionText: Before buying snacks, Mariam checks the ingredients, thinks about why she wants them, and controls the amount she eats. This practice is called ......... .
mcq.explanation: Deliberately assessing necessity and health value is mindful consumption.

mcq.questionText: Enough sleep after hard exercise is essential for ......... .
mcq.explanation: Sleep allows physiological and muscular recovery.

mcq.questionText: Regular exercise and healthy eating ......... our physical health throughout our lives.
mcq.explanation: Positive lifestyle choices shape long-term health.

mcq.questionText: Learning relaxation techniques can help students ......... exam pressure.
mcq.explanation: 'Cope with' means to manage stressful challenges effectively.

mcq.questionText: The school plans to ......... a new support group for stressed students.
mcq.explanation: 'Set up' means to establish or organize.

mcq.questionText: Lack of sleep can ......... serious problems with concentration and memory.
mcq.explanation: 'Lead to' means to cause or result in.

correctForm.prompt: The two teams played ......... (competitive) until the final whistle.
correctForm.explanation: Modifying the verb 'played' requires the adverb 'competitively'.

correctForm.prompt: Doctors say people often ......... (underestimation) how much sleep affects mood and memory.
Researchers found ......... (measure) improvements in stress levels after weeks of mindfulness practice.
Eating too much ......... (process) food can lead to fatigue and poor concentration.
Teachers encourage students to stay ......... (mind) of their thoughts during stressful exam periods.
Regular exercise is highly ......... (benefit) for both physical and mental health.
Teenagers who ......... (consumption) high-caffeine drinks regularly often report trouble sleeping.
correctForm.explanation: Relative clause verb in present tense requires 'consume'.

correctForm.prompt: Students who ......... (annotation) their notes tend to remember lesson content more easily.
correctForm.explanation: Plural subject relative clause verb requires 'annotate'.

correctForm.prompt: It is difficult to ......... (concentration) in class after a poor night's sleep.
A ......... (nourish) diet is essential for healthy brain development during the teenage years.

skillsWriting.questionText: The main purpose of an analytical paragraph is to ......... an idea using reasons, evidence, and explanation.
skillsWriting.explanation: An analytical paragraph examines an argument methodically.

skillsWriting.questionText: The first sentence of an analytical paragraph should usually present a clear ......... .
skillsWriting.explanation: The topic sentence presents the primary claim or assertion.

skillsWriting.questionText: The expression 'This is because ...' is most suitable for introducing the ......... .
skillsWriting.explanation: 'This is because...' gives the underlying logical rationale.

skillsWriting.questionText: The main purpose of evidence is to ......... the writer's claim.
skillsWriting.explanation: Evidence supplies factual and research backing.

skillsWriting.questionText: The word 'Therefore' is most commonly used to introduce a/an ......... .
skillsWriting.explanation: 'Therefore' introduces the logical conclusion or synthesis.

skillsWriting.questionText: The correct structure is Claim -> Reason -> Evidence -> ......... -> Conclusion.
skillsWriting.explanation: Explanation connects the evidence back to the central claim.

grammarStructures.titleAr: عبارات الوصل وضمائر الوصل (who, which, that, where, when, whose, whom)
grammarStructures.summaryAr: تستخدم ضمائر الوصل لربط الجمل وتحديد الأسماء أو إضافة معلومات إضافية عنها.

rules.usage: يشير إلى الفاعل أو المفعول العاقل (people)
يشير إلى الأشياء والحيوانات والأفكار غير العاقلة (things / animals)
يشير إلى المكان إذا كانت الجملة تعبر عما يحدث فيه (مكان حدوث الفعل)
يشير إلى الملكية (يأتي بعده اسم مملوك للاسم السابق له)
يشير إلى المفعول به العاقل فقط (خاصة بعد حروف الجر مثل with whom, to whom)

exercises.questionText: The man ......... fixed our car is very kind.
exercises.explanation: 'The man' is a person doing the action, requiring 'who'.

exercises.questionText: She is the girl ......... brother plays football with me.
exercises.explanation: 'Brother' belongs to the girl, denoting possession (whose brother).

exercises.questionText: The book ......... I bought is interesting.
The guest house ......... we stayed had a very friendly owner.
exercises.explanation: The guest house is the place where staying occurred.

exercises.questionText: My aunt, ......... I visited in the hospital, is getting better now.
exercises.explanation: My aunt is the object of 'visited', appropriately taking 'whom' (or who in informal).

exercises.questionText: Only one sentence in each group is grammatically correct:
options: Teenagers who practice mindfulness often manage stress more effectively.
Teenagers which practice mindfulness often manage stress more effectively.
Teenagers practicing mindfulness, they often manage stress more effectively.
Practicing mindfulness, stress manages teenagers more effectively.
exercises.correctAnswer: Teenagers who practice mindfulness often manage stress more effectively.
exercises.explanation: Teenagers are people and require 'who'; the other options contain dangling modifiers or wrong pronouns.

grammarStructures.titleAr: صيغ اسم الفاعل واسم المفعول (Participle Clauses)
grammarStructures.summaryAr: تستخدم Present Participles (-ing) للفاعل النشط، و Past Participles (-ed / V3) للمبني للمجهول، و Having + V3 لاختصار أحداث متتالية تم أحدها قبل الآخر.

rules.usage: يحل محل جملة معلوم تبدأ بـ When/While/Because لنفس الفاعل
يحل محل جملة مجهول مبنية للمفعول (Passive reduction)
يحل محل After + Past Perfect (حدث اكتمل أولاً قبل الحدث الثاني)

exercises.questionText: ......... the traffic lights turn red, the driver stopped the car at once.
exercises.explanation: Active action simultaneous with stopping: 'Seeing the lights turn red...'

exercises.questionText: The bridge, ......... many years ago, is still standing strong today.
exercises.explanation: Passive reduction: The bridge (which was) built many years ago.

exercises.questionText: ......... his work early, Amir decided to go for a walk.
exercises.explanation: Having + V3 signifies completion of work prior to taking a walk.

grammarStructures.summaryAr: قواعد If الشرطية (First, Second, Third) وقواعد القلب (Inversion) باستخدام Were, Had, Should بدلاً من If.

rules.usage: بديل If في الحالة الثانية: Were I you, I would apologize.
بديل If في الحالة الثالثة: Had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
بديل If في الحالة الأولى والثانية: Should it rain, we will stay at home.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses inversion instead of 'if'?
options: I were you, I would apologize.
Was I you, I would apologize.
If I was you, I would apologize, were I.
Were I you, I would apologize.
exercises.correctAnswer: Were I you, I would apologize.
exercises.explanation: 'Were I you' is the correct inversion of 'If I were you'.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses inversion in a third conditional?
options: Have I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
If had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
Had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
Had I know the truth, I would have acted differently.
exercises.correctAnswer: Had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + Subject + V3' replaces 'If + Subject + had + V3'.
